chapter: New York with Lester Young and Coleman Hawkins
title: Hawkins the teacher; touring with him to Billy Berg's
summary: Hawkins taught chord progressions at his piano and hi-fi, and Thompson played with him on records and a tour ending at Billy Berg's in California.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And they had entirely different styles, but as I said, Coleman Hawkins was more of a teacher, because he'd sit down to the piano and show you what chord progressions he wanted, and he dealt in these chord progressions and he's a great listener of classical music. And he had expensive equipment in his -- he was one of the first people I remember hearing in New York who had an expensive hi-fi equipment when it first came out, you know. And this type of thing. He had an expensive baby grand piano in his apartment. He had the things necessary and to show another musician what was happening in this field of music. And he could express it, he could play it, and he could teach it, and he knew what he was doing, and he had the depth that was -- just incomparable. Like ballads. ballots. You know, the man could play a ballad like Art Tatum played on the piano, and he could invert these chords and he could get so much expression in them, you know. So I always considered Coleman Hawkins like a college of music, and my playing with him was I'd say one of the highlights of my life. I played with him in New York, and we made some

records, in New York, and we travelled -- toured the country, a brief tour of the midwestern states, and on to California where we played in Billy Berg's famous jazz club. And we were considered to be one of the first organized groups to play the type of music that we were playing, which was considered to be modern, although it really wasn't that modern in the sense, but that's the way they referred to it.
